log.title: Heavy attacks, lighter crates, bigger skill web
changes: Hold the attack button to wind up a heavy attack (a bar fills over your head), then release for up to 2.1x damage, a bigger swing, harder knockback and a short hit-stop. A quick click is still a fast strike.
Scroll the mouse wheel to cycle through your weapons and tools (fists included). A quick picker shows what you're holding.
Object weight now comes from size and material: crates are easy to lift and toss, barrels a bit heavier, rocks and rubble dense. Your strength makes dragging easier.
10 new skills (2-3 per branch): Clotting, Vitality, Parkour, Sprinter, Nimble Fingers, Lanternwright, Composure, Silver Tongue, Brawler and Pack Mule.
Skill web: branches stay closed until you click one, which zooms in on just that branch. Clicking a cell selects it and shows a Confirm upgrade button, so you never spend a point by accident.

log.title: Blood & Physics
changes: Physics melee: your melee weapon (or fists) is held toward your cursor all the time. Damage comes from how fast the blade or head is actually moving, so whipping the mouse across someone hurts. Click to strike: knives, shivs and fists thrust, heavier weapons do a big overhead swing. Heavy weapons swing slower but hit harder, and blunt ones bounce off on impact. Enemies fight the same way.

Bullets are real projectiles: they travel, drop a little, punch through bodies, ricochet off rock at shallow angles, shove ragdolls and loose objects, and spray blood out the exit side. Muzzle flashes and ejected casings too.

Gore (scales with the Gore setting): limbs get cut, blown or shot off and fly around as physics objects with bone stumps, heads can come off, torsos spill intestines and organs (heart, lungs, liver, kidneys, stomach) that flop and bleed, bodies get stained where they were hit, and corpses keep bleeding into growing pools. Losing a leg puts you on the ground, losing an arm cripples your swing. Explosions tear people apart, and you can hack at or shoot corpses.
Faster combat: shorter melee cooldowns, faster gun fire and reloads, and enemies aim and fire sooner.
Movement: walking is about 50% faster and running is a real feature (about 2x walking speed). Hold Shift or double-tap a direction to run, and running drains stamina more slowly.
New animations: proper walk and run cycles with planted steps, bending knees and counter-swinging arms. Running leans forward with pumping arms and kicks up dust, and landings squash.

log.title: Honeycomb skill web
changes: Skill web redesigned as a honeycomb: wax cells fill with dripping honey as you unlock ranks, category cells fill up with honey too, the hub is now the striped Vespa, and the colors are warm cave tones. Labels no longer overlap and the big hexes no longer cover each other.
The depth meter now sits under your portrait, and its text no longer clips into the bar.
Every host's portrait gets its own background color.

Glass shards no longer appear all over the caves (none in the Mossy Grotto, rare patches in the Crystal Depths). The ones that remain are bright, outlined, glinting and lit, so you can see them coming.

log.title: Taller, more detailed characters
changes: Every human is now drawn taller with more pixels, closer to People Playground proportions: a square head with nose, eye and brow, a longer torso with a belt, slim outlined arms and legs, hands and boots. Hair, beards, helmets, masks, backpacks and weapons were redrawn to match.

log.title: Wall parkour, lanterns & rebindable keys
changes: Every keybind can be changed in Settings: click a key, press the new one (Del clears, Esc cancels). Each action has two slots and a reset button. On-screen hints update to match.
Volume sliders now use the game's honey colors and follow the selected UI theme.
Hex menu rebuilt: the hexes no longer overlap and every button's name is printed inside it.
Wall parkour: hold toward a wall in mid-air to slide down it, press Jump to kick off the other way, and Sprint+Jump into a wall to boost up it (twice per jump). You can chain wall jumps up shafts.
The flashlight is now a small oil lantern hanging at your waist. It sways as you move and lights all around you instead of a cone. Batteries are now Lantern Oil.
Every human now carries a waist lantern: raiders, soldiers, traders and townsfolk (the cave-mad wretches don't). You can see them coming, and they light you up too.
Fall damage reduced by 30%.

log.title: Centered title screen
changes: The logo and main menu are now centered on every screen width, including ultrawide.

log.title: The Vespa
changes: New lore: you are a Vespa, a parasite from an interstellar hive mind, riding human hosts deeper and deeper into the caves. That's why every host is a random new person.
Full prologue cutscene on your first game (replay it from the title screen). Click or Space to advance, Esc to skip.
Your host's eyes glow gold and leave a fading trail. The glow cuts through total darkness so you always know which one is you.

Relic flowers grow deeper down. Their nectar awakens one of 8 Vespa gifts: Overclocked Heart, Chitin Plating, Compound Sight, Stinger Lash, Wing Buds (glide), Hive Pulse [X], Amber Blood and Mandibles.
When your host dies, the Vespa bursts out as a tendril-lashing goo for 10 seconds. Take them with you.
No more extraction. A town waits every 250m with an inn bed (rest & save), a doctor, a trader, a well, a workbench and a Deep Post that sends your loot up to Base Camp.

Online co-op: pick 'Descend with a partner' at the lift, share a 5-letter room code and go down together. Shared cave and enemies. Each player keeps their own save, and reloading reconnects automatically. In co-op a dead player's Vespa drifts to their partner and takes a new host.
Save slots (3) and autosave: every few seconds, when you rest, and whenever you close or reload the page. Reloading drops you right back where you were.
Destructible terrain: dig through rock with a Pickaxe, Ice Axe or Rock Hammer (aim at the rock and click). Dynamite blows holes in walls. Both can be found, bought and crafted.
Ropes: jump off them any time, climb about 60% faster, and Shift+S slides down fast. Press W mid-air to grab one.
Walking into a low gap now drops you into a crawl automatically, so crawlspaces stop snagging you.
Objects have real weight: heavy crates fall hard, drag slowly and can't be lifted high. Crates no longer launch themselves at you or do big damage. Dragged objects barely hurt.
Guns hit harder (pistol 46, rifle 84) and headshots deal 1.5x.
Generative background music for the title, prologue, Base Camp, each biome, towns and the death burst. The ambient drone is gone.
New colored anime-style pixel portraits that blink, plus 30+ hairstyles across men and women.
Redesigned title screen with a clear menu: Continue/New Game, Save Slots, Settings, then Prologue, Run Archive and Update Log.
Modern glassy HUD: new bottom-left vitals card, hotbar, depth gauge and portrait card.
7 UI themes in Settings (Honey, Abyss Blue, Moss, Ember, Amethyst, Hive Contrast, Bone & Ink) and new rounded volume sliders.
Livelier caves: fireflies, sand motes, snow, crystal glints and embers drift around. Biomes are a bit less dark, and the grotto has far fewer spores.
Backpacks, outfits and all new items now use Pixel Atlas icons.

log.title: Into the Caves
changes: Nectar's End is now a cave-diving game: organic caves with uneven floors, stalactites, rock ledges, ropes down, risky open pits and crawlspaces.

Five cave biomes, each with a perk and a challenge: Mossy Grotto (forage mushrooms & herbs / spores, damp wounds), Sunscorched Sandstone (dry air, ruins & prickly pears / heat & sinking sand), Frozen Hollows (cold slows bleeding, fresh water / hypothermia, slippery ice, falling icicles), Crystal Depths (glowing crystals, Crystal Shards / crystal radiation, shard floors) and Magma Abyss (no cold, richest caches / heat, lava, steam vents).
Walk up small cave steps automatically.
New items: Cave Mushroom, Healing Herb, Prickly Pear, Glowcap (throwable light), Rock; cave-themed weapons and gear.
All item, menu and skill icons replaced with CC0 Pixel Atlas sprites.
Base Camp lobby, winch lifts, expedition camps, triage tents, mine storerooms and research outposts.
New cave title screen.

log.title: Update notifications & update log
changes: New versions now announce themselves with a popup: Update now, or it auto-updates after a countdown.
Added this Update Log (title screen, Settings, and the update popup).
"What's new" opens automatically the first time you load a new version.
Pain rebalanced: wounds hurt less constantly, threshold raised to 60.

log.title: First playable build
changes: Title screen, Staging Lobby with Skill Terminal, Gear Locker, Quartermaster and Survivor Dossier.
Random human survivor every run: name, age, occupation, traits and looks.
Endless descent through four biomes with a depth meter and extraction elevators every 250m.
Limb-by-limb anatomy, organs, bleeding, fractures, infection, pain and blackouts; triage by body part.
Loose verlet physics: ragdolls, props, debris, throwables, right-click dragging.
Hex menu (M), fading-ink portrait, hex skill web, crafting, map, journal, cemetery.
Ultrawide support up to 32:9.
